ip_top_stories.title: Millions of Copyrighted Songs Were Fed to AI Music Generators – Now There's Proof
ip_top_stories.summary: An Atlantic investigation has surfaced evidence that millions of copyrighted songs were used to train AI music generators, providing concrete proof of data provenance issues in the AI music industry. The discovery is directly relevant to ongoing litigation against AI music platforms including Suno. A July court ruling is expected in the Suno case following discovery disclosures.

ip_top_stories.title: Meta can't dodge porn producer's copyright claims over AI training
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has ruled that Meta cannot avoid copyright infringement claims brought by a pornography producer over the use of its content to train AI models. The ruling follows a separate embarrassing disclosure in which Meta was found to have mass-downloaded thousands of pirated adult films for AI training purposes. The decisions represent a significant development in AI training data litigation.

ip_top_stories.title: Publishers Sue WeLib for Copyright Infringement [Metered]
ip_top_stories.summary: A group of publishers has filed a lawsuit against pirate site WeLib for copyright infringement. The case adds to a growing body of publisher-led legal action targeting unauthorised distribution of books, with implications for how such repositories intersect with AI training data supply chains.

ip_top_stories.title: AI, Research Drive Gains at Wiley in Fiscal 2026 [Metered]
ip_top_stories.summary: Wiley reported financial gains in fiscal 2026, attributing growth partly to AI-related research activity and licensing opportunities. The results reflect broader publisher strategies to monetise content through AI partnerships and data licensing deals.

ip_top_stories.title: Who Owns the Code Claude Wrote?
ip_top_stories.summary: An analysis examines the unresolved question of copyright ownership in code generated by AI systems such as Anthropic's Claude, exploring how current law fails to clearly assign authorship or ownership to AI-generated outputs. The piece highlights the growing practical urgency of the issue for developers and businesses relying on AI-generated code.

ip_further_links.title: AI Copyright Law Lags; Parliament Must Act on AI-Generated Content
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary argues that existing copyright law is inadequate to address AI-generated content and calls on Parliament to introduce new legislation to close the gap.

ip_further_links.title: Weighing up AI prompts with copyright law
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis considers how copyright law applies to AI prompts, examining whether prompts themselves can attract protection and how they interact with the outputs they generate.

ip_further_links.title: Researchers propose 'copyleft' rules for generative AI
ip_further_links.summary: Researchers have put forward a framework applying copyleft-style licensing principles to generative AI systems, aiming to ensure that training data rights are respected and outputs remain open.

ip_further_links.title: Movement for Open Web (MOW) launches 'Search only Contract' over AI Harvesting
ip_further_links.summary: The Movement for Open Web has launched a new contractual framework aimed at restricting AI crawlers from harvesting web content beyond search indexing purposes.

ip_further_links.title: Trademark Law Meets Generative AI: Key Takeaways from the Getty v. Stability AI Ruling
ip_further_links.summary: A legal commentary examines trademark law implications arising from the Getty Images v. Stability AI ruling, drawing out key lessons for how generative AI outputs may infringe trademark as well as copyright.

ip_further_links.title: Publishers Reframe AI From Risk to Growth Strategy
ip_further_links.summary: An industry report finds that publishers are increasingly repositioning AI from a threat to their business into a strategic growth opportunity, particularly around licensing and operational efficiency.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the patent industry: Bubble trouble and the affordability myth
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat examines claims that AI is transforming the patent industry, questioning whether the productivity gains are overstated and whether AI tools are genuinely affordable for smaller practitioners.

ip_further_links.title: Academic Freedom for the Win; Open Access Mandate in Germany Declared Unconstitutional
ip_further_links.summary: Germany's open access mandate has been declared unconstitutional on academic freedom grounds, in a ruling with significant implications for open access policy and academic publishing in Europe.

ip_further_links.title: At the AUPresses Conference, Publishers Strive for Durability and Trust [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: University press publishers at the AUPresses annual conference discussed strategies for long-term sustainability and maintaining reader trust in an era of AI-generated content and shifting research publishing norms.

ip_further_links.title: Spotlight: Opportunities for AI in Publishing Operations [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: A Publishers Weekly sponsored spotlight explores how publishers are deploying AI tools to streamline operational workflows, from rights management to content production.
